objective: Define the narrow parser integer hardening boundary after the scoped parser-only smoke result, without claiming a patch fix, sidecar handoff, RTL execution, timing, arbitrary RTL/filelist support, or automatic allocation.

definition_decision.weakest_point: The accepted parser-only smoke covers selected positive values and zero-count rejection, but the overlay patch still parses counts with std::atoi. That means non-numeric suffixes such as 64abc are not strict integer evidence, and dash-prefixed negative values need an explicit tokenization-safe boundary before broader native-parser, sidecar-handoff, or upstream-quality claims.
reason: the previous review accepted only scoped parser accept/reject behavior and explicitly left strict integer parsing as a non-claim
the current overlay patch uses std::atoi in V3Options.cpp, which can accept numeric prefixes and cannot prove strict integer-token validation
zero-count rejection is already covered by the parser-behavior smoke and should not be confused with negative-count or suffix hardening
sidecar handoff would broaden the workstream before the known parser-token weakness is defined

allowed_only_if: source build gate remains the reproducible authority
run gate records the exact binary path as generated evidence only

allowed_binary_sources.allowed_when: the generated binary is absent or stale

generated_smoke_rtl.path_policy: reuse or regenerate the trivial lint-only RTL under artifacts/verilator_native_option_parser_overlay_patch_parser_behavior/

hardening_boundary.expected_hardened_failure_policy: nonzero exit code with stderr containing the expected strict integer diagnostic after the patch is hardened

required_hardening_cases.name: reject_negative_states_separate_token
required_hardening_cases.reason: This is the source-review candidate input. If the Verilator tokenizer rejects '-1' before the value callback, a run gate must record that as tokenizer behavior, not strict integer hardening.

required_hardening_cases.name: reject_negative_steps_separate_token
required_hardening_cases.reason: This is the source-review candidate input. If the Verilator tokenizer rejects '-1' before the value callback, a run gate must record that as tokenizer behavior, not strict integer hardening.

required_hardening_cases.name: reject_non_numeric_states_suffix
required_hardening_cases.reason: std::atoi can parse the numeric prefix 64, so this case requires stricter token consumption before a strict integer claim.

required_hardening_cases.name: reject_non_numeric_steps_suffix
required_hardening_cases.reason: std::atoi can parse the numeric prefix 1, so this case requires stricter token consumption before a strict integer claim.

equals_form_negative_values.reason: Equals form may help isolate value validation from dash-prefixed tokenization, but the first hardening definition keeps the source-review separate-token candidates as required cases.
